# Document The Rising ToneForge SFX in SFX_CONVENTION.md (full game audio profile)

## Goal

As an engine maintainer, I want The Rising's ToneForge-generated face-off SFX
documented as a first-class game audio profile in the shared
`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md`, so sibling game repos have a complete, copyable
reference for the convention (keys, deterministic regeneration, runtime wiring,
fallback behaviour).

## Problem statement

`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` documents the `sfx-` key convention, asset
organisation, playback helpers and collision protection, and it carries one
ToneForge precedent section (`## Main Street Synth SFX`). The Rising already
ships three ToneForge-generated face-off sounds, but the shared convention has
no The Rising entry — so the doc is incomplete for sibling repos and the
game-side knowledge lives only in `tce-the-rising/README.md`.

## Existing state

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` (in this repo) has no The Rising section, and the
  `## Audio Asset Organization` tree lists `default/`, `golf/`, `sushi-go/`,
  `feudalism/`, `beleaguered-castle/`, `lost-cities/`, `main-street/` — no
  `the-rising/`.
- The Rising keeps its audio in its **own** repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), loaded through the
  pinned `core` submodule; no assets are vendored into the engine.
- The game README (§ *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) already records the
  authoritative facts:
  - `sfx-face-off-reveal` → `face-off-reveal.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-treasure-reveal --seed 42`
  - `sfx-float-in-whoosh` → `float-in-whoosh.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe whoosh-air-swish --seed 43`
  - `sfx-land-tick` → `land-tick.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-timer-tick --seed 44`
  - keys in `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file
    mappings in `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, preloaded via `preload()` +
    `audioPathWithFallback`, played only via `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound`.
- The game plays all three beats when reduced motion is enabled (no travel, but
  audio still fires).
- The Rising has **no** ToneForge synth mapping module (unlike Main Street's
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts`) — playback falls through to
  committed WAV assets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` gains a `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section
  documenting the three keys, their asset filenames under
  `public/assets/audio/the-rising/`, and the exact deterministic
  `tf generate --recipe <recipe> --seed <int> --output <path>` command for each
  (seeds 42 / 43 / 44 as recorded in the game README).
- AC2 — The `## Audio Asset Organization` tree gains a `the-rising/` entry
  noting the assets live in the game repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), mirroring the existing
  Main Street parenthetical.
- AC3 — The profile records runtime wiring: keys declared in
  `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file mappings in
  `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, loading through `preload()` +
  `audioPathWithFallback()`, playback only through
  `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound` (`no-direct-sound-play` rule).
- AC4 — The profile records reduced-motion behaviour: with reduced motion
  enabled the face-off animation is instant but all three SFX beats still play.
- AC5 — The profile states fallback behaviour: the three face-off WAVs are
  game-specific with no `default/` equivalent, the nine baseline SFX fall back
  to `default/`, and there is no ToneForge synth mapping for The Rising (so
  playback resolves to WAV assets).
- AC6 — The profile links the game-side reproducibility instructions
  (`tce-the-rising/README.md` § *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) and states the
  section is maintained in the engine because sibling game repos read this doc.
- AC7 — Documentation-only change: no engine code, constants or behaviour is
  altered, and `npm run build` + `npm test` pass on the docs branch.
- AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Docs-only: no engine code behaviour change; no new engine SFX keys.
- Do not copy The Rising's WAV assets into the engine repo (assets stay in the
  game repo, referenced by path).
- Only `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` is expected to change; `CHANGELOG.md` is managed
  by the release pipeline.
- Landed on engine `dev` through the normal flow. Producer decision
  (2026-10-19): the consuming game repo (`tce-the-rising`) pins its `core`
  submodule to the **`dev` commit containing this change**, rather than waiting
  for the `dev` → `main` release promotion — so the commit SHA must be reported
  on completion for the cross-repo pointer bump.

## Key Files

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` — new `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section; add
  `the-rising/` to the `## Audio Asset Organization` tree.

## Related work

- Cross-repo tracker: **RISE-0MVBUSQUR006LPVP** (tce-the-rising) — blocked by
  this item; on completion it bumps its `core` submodule pointer to this item's
  engine `dev` commit and verifies the doc renders in-tree. Report the commit
  SHA in the completion comment so the game-side bump is deterministic.
- `RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH` (tce-the-rising) — generated the three WAVs and
  recorded the recipes/seeds this section documents.
- Precedent: `## Main Street Synth SFX` in the same doc, and
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` for the synth-mapping contrast.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (drift):** recipes/seeds recorded in the game README could diverge from
  this section. Mitigation: quote the exact commands and link the README section
  as the authority.
- **Risk (inverted dependency):** documenting another repo's assets in the
  engine could imply the engine owns them. Mitigation: state explicitly that
  assets live in the game repo and the engine only owns the convention text.
- **Assumption:** the three recipe names/seeds in the game README are the
  committed, reproducible values (verified there; recorded in
  RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH as byte-identical on regeneration).
- **Assumption:** a docs-only engine change still needs the normal
  build+test gate, per engine policy.

# Intake Brief — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

**Work item:** CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

## Problem statement

When a release is cut from a game repo such as `tce-main-street`, the game ends up versioned with the Tableau-Card-Engine (core) version number. Each game repo must maintain its **own** independent version, decoupled from the core's release cadence.

## Users / user stories

- **Game maintainers (agents + operators)** cutting a release of a sibling game repo:
  "As a maintainer of `tce-main-street`, I want the game's release version to reflect the
  game's own release history, so players can tell the game version apart from the engine version."
- **Players and testers** reading the version label on the game selector / game screens:
  "As a playtester, I want the version I report in feedback to identify the game build
  (and be meaningful on its own), not silently mirror the engine version."
- **Engine maintainers** composing the multi-repo distribution:
  "As an engine maintainer, I want a game's release version to be independent of the
  engine's, so engine releases and game releases can proceed at different cadences."

## Root-cause analysis (evidence)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` writes the game repo's
  `package.json` with `version: manifest.version ?? '0.0.0'`, where `manifest` is the
  **core's** `package.json` (`readCoreManifest(coreRoot)`). A new or re-scaffolded game
  therefore inherits the core's current version number.
- The behaviour is pinned by a test: `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  asserts `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` (the stubbed core manifest version).
- Observed in the wild: every `tce-*` sibling carries a core-derived version —
  0.1.17 for the batch scaffolded 2026-09-26 (the core version at that date), and
  0.1.21 for `main-street` / `the-rising`, whose releases tracked the core's version
  patch-for-patch (core v0.1.17→v0.1.21, main-street v0.1.17→v0.1.21).
- **Not the cause:** the ship skill's `bump-version.js` resolves the **invoking repo's**
  root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and bumps that `package.json`, so once a
  game repo carries its own version its releases bump correctly. The coupling is
  seeded at scaffold time and then persists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No core-version coupling in the scaffold.** `renderPackageJson()` no longer derives
   the game's version from the core manifest: a freshly scaffolded game repo's
   `package.json` `version` is the independent baseline `0.1.0` (producer decision), and
   a re-scaffold of an existing game repo **preserves** the version already in that
   repo's `package.json` rather than overwriting it.
2. **Existing game repos are not renumbered.** The work does not rewrite sibling game
   repo versions: `golf` / `blackjack` / `coloretto` / `feudalism` / `lost-cities` /
   `sushi-go` / `beleaguered-castle` (0.1.17), `the-rising` (0.1.21) and `main-street`
   (0.1.21) keep their current numbers and diverge naturally on their next release.
   A re-scaffold of any of them is version-neutral (verified for at least one repo, or
   covered by the unit-test preserve case).
3. **Scope limited to the scaffold seeding path, with the ship path verified.** Only the
   scaffold seeding + its tests/docs change; a verification note records that the ship
   `bump-version.js` reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` (no shared/release-code
   change required). Any newly discovered version-leak path is filed as a follow-up work
   item rather than folded into this one.
4. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a new-game scaffold seeds `0.1.0`; (b) a re-scaffold
   of an existing repo preserves its version; (c) no test asserts core-version coupling
   (the `'9.9.9'` assertion is replaced). Tests must exercise real `package.json`
   read/write behaviour, not merely assert rendered strings in isolation.
5. **Documentation.** The per-game version policy is documented (each game owns its
   version; the scaffold seeds `0.1.0` and preserves on re-scaffold; a game release bumps
   only that game's version) in the new-game guide and/or the multi-repo architecture
   scaffold section.
6. **Quality gates.** `npm test -- --project unit` and `npm run build` pass with the
   change; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not edit the global ship skill or any `skill/` tree (`AGENTS.md` repository
  boundary); the bump logic is already repo-local and needs verification only.
- Push to `dev` only. Cross-repo game changes (if any) are recorded on this core work
  item or in the game repo's own Worklog store.
- `renderPackageJson` stays a pure render function: the preserve-on-re-scaffold decision
  must be injected/explicit (e.g. an existing-version parameter or a read in
  `scaffoldGameRepo`), keeping the template unit-testable.
- Do not add a hard-coded per-game version table — the policy is generic.

## Existing state

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` is the single generator for every `tce-<game>` repo
  `package.json`; it is invoked via `npm run scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` (core),
  `npm run scaffold` (game repos) and `scripts/setup-distribution.ts`.
- `ScaffoldOptions` carries `coreManifest?: CoreManifest`; `CoreManifest.version` is
  typed optional and only used for the game version stamp.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` has a `renderPackageJson` describe block
  and a `scaffoldGameRepo` integration block using a temp sibling layout.
- Game repos carry `__APP_VERSION__` injected from **their own** `package.json` in their
  `vite.config.ts` (generated by the same scaffold), so display follows the package
  version automatically once seeding is fixed.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` in each game repo records the engine **commit** (not a
  version), so engine/game version independence has no other data coupling.

## Desired change

- Seed a new game repo at `0.1.0`; preserve an existing repo's version on re-scaffold.
- Keep `renderPackageJson` pure and explicit about the version it writes.
- Replace the core-version-coupling test with baseline + preserve coverage.
- Document the per-game version policy (who owns a game's version, how a release bumps
  it, and why it is not the engine version).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` (drop `manifest.version`; take an explicit version), `ScaffoldOptions`, `scaffoldGameRepo()` (read the existing `package.json` version before writing).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — replace `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` with baseline + preserve cases; add a re-scaffold integration case against a temp repo with an existing version.
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — §3 scaffold stage: state the seeded baseline and that games own their version.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "Per-game repo scaffold": version-ownership note alongside the existing `package.json` description.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Build-Time Version Injection: clarify the label shows the **composing repo's** version (game repo ⇒ game version, core ⇒ engine version).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — re-scaffold clobbers a released version.** If the preserve path reads the
  wrong file or a stale path, a re-scaffold could reset a game to `0.1.0` and break
  tag↔version correlation. *Mitigation:* preserve is read-then-write inside
  `scaffoldGameRepo` with an integration test on a temp repo that has an existing
  version; unreadable/missing `package.json` falls back to the `0.1.0` baseline.
- **Risk — tests only assert rendered strings** (the existing test's weakness) so the
  real write path stays unguarded. *Mitigation:* AC4 requires integration-level
  coverage of the write path.
- **Risk — scope creep into release tooling.** "Fix the version" invites touching the
  ship skill, CI, or renumbering every game. *Mitigation:* Q3 decision constrains scope
  to the scaffold seeding path; any additional leak found is a follow-up work item.
- **Assumption — `0.1.0` baseline is acceptable before any release exists** (producer
  decision Q1); the first release from a new game therefore tags `v0.1.1` after the
  ship patch bump. Documented rather than special-cased.
- **Assumption — leaving existing versions in place is safe** (producer decision Q2):
  released `main-street` tags `v0.1.18`–`v0.1.21` stay valid; games diverge from the
  engine's numbering at their next release.
- **Assumption — no other core-version coupling exists** (producer decision Q3): the
  ship bump path reads the invoking repo's `package.json`; verified, not modified.

## Related work

### Automated report (find-related)

- **CG-0MSQBQSCX006R02B** — CLI draft-release script (code + docs) (completed)
- **CG-0MM1OQ5U80HVOPKJ** — Inconsistent move validation patterns across games (completed, tangential)
- **CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R** — Local skill: promote Windows Setup artifact to GitHub release (operator-approved) (completed)
- Repository file matches: `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (generic keyword matches)

### Manually linked context

- **CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W** — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed): established the version display surface that makes the coupling visible.
- **CG-0MUI9K4F8009DYJL** — Add an ALPHA banner and version number to all game screens (completed): same display surface.
- **CG-0MRZ35LK80064WIS** / **CG-0MRZ0YNCO003J5CN** — CI-3 release checklist (completed): release-cadence context.
- Source: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` in `../tce-main-street` (engine pin vs dev sync — the only other engine/game coupling data).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Initial version baseline for a brand-new game repo

**Question:** When the scaffold creates a **new** game repo (no prior `package.json`), should the game start at `0.1.0`, `0.0.0`, or another baseline?
**Recommended:** `0.1.0` — matches the existing `0.1.x` convention, gives a sensible first release (`v0.1.1`) without implying engine compatibility.
**Answer (producer):** `0.1.0`. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q2 — Existing game repos: renumber now vs leave in place

**Question:** Should existing sibling game repos (currently core-derived: 0.1.17, or 0.1.21 for `main-street`/`the-rising`) be renumbered as part of this work, or left at their current numbers and decoupled from here?
**Recommended:** leave in place — released tags (`main-street` v0.1.18–v0.1.21) already exist; renumbering would orphan tag/version correlation for little benefit.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — leave in place. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q3 — Scope of the version leak

**Question:** Intake identified the root cause as `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson()` stamping the core manifest version into game `package.json` (pinned by `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` asserting `pkg.version === '9.9.9'`). Are other paths in scope — e.g. a release accidentally run from the core checkout, or the distribution/launcher build stamping the core version onto games?
**Recommended:** scaffold seeding + test/doc updates only (the ship `bump-version.js` already reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), with the ship path verified rather than modified.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — scaffold seeding + tests/docs only; verify the ship path. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

> Research note for Q3: inspected `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js`
> (`PKG_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'package.json')`, `REPO_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel`),
> `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (same repo-local bump), `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (pins a commit SHA in
> `configs/engine-pin.json`, no version), and each game's generated `vite.config.ts`
> (`__APP_VERSION__` from the game's own `package.json`) — no additional version-leak path found.

---

## Plan (created by the plan skill, 2026-10-22)

**Decision: single-item plan — no child work items.** The whole change (code +
tests + docs) is one small end-to-end slice that a single implement session can
deliver; child items would add coordination overhead without isolating any
independently shippable behaviour. Effort Small / risk Medium (effort-and-risk
report on this item). Test-first ordering is preserved within the single slice.

### Slices (executed in order within the implement session)

**A. Tests first (red) — `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`**
- `renderPackageJson`: a new game renders `version: '0.1.0'` even when the core
  manifest stub declares `9.9.9` (proves decoupling); an explicit version
  argument is written verbatim. Delete the `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')`
  assertion.
- `scaffoldGameRepo` integration over the temp sibling fixture, asserting real
  on-disk read/write: (a) a **new** game repo is seeded with `0.1.0`; (b) a
  re-scaffold of a repo whose `package.json` already says `0.1.17` **preserves**
  `0.1.17`; (c) a missing/unparseable existing `package.json` falls back to
  `0.1.0`.
- Verify red: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  fails for the expected reasons.

**B. Scaffold seeding (green) — `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`**
- Add `export const GAME_INITIAL_VERSION = '0.1.0';` with a comment stating the
  per-game version policy (each game owns its version; decoupled from the core).
- `renderPackageJson(game, manifest, coreRel, version = GAME_INITIAL_VERSION)`:
  write the explicit `version` verbatim; never read `manifest.version`. Keep the
  render function pure — the version is injected (constraint).
- Add `readExistingPackageVersion(gameRepoRoot): string | undefined` — total:
  returns the string `version` from `<root>/package.json`, `undefined` when the
  file is absent, unreadable, or has no string version.
- `ScaffoldOptions.version?: string` explicit override (wins over preserve),
  resolved as `options.version ?? readExistingPackageVersion(root) ??
  GAME_INITIAL_VERSION`.
- `ScaffoldResult` gains `version: string` + `versionSource` (`'explicit'` |
  `'preserved'` | `'baseline'`) and the CLI prints `version: <v> (<source>)`.
- `CoreManifest.version` stays typed (a package.json subset) but is documented
  as unused by the scaffold, so test stubs can keep declaring it to prove
  decoupling.
- Verify green: targeted unit tests + `npm run build`.

**C. Documentation**
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` §3 — seeded baseline `0.1.0`, preserve on
  re-scaffold, games own their version (AC5).
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 — `package.json` bullet: version
  ownership note (AC5).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Build-Time Version Injection (§) — clarify
  `__APP_VERSION__` shows the **composing repo's** version: game repo ⇒ game
  version, core ⇒ engine version; a game release bumps only that game's version.

**D. Verification note + gates (AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7)**
- Verification note on the work item: the ship `bump-version.js` resolves
  `REPO_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and bumps `PKG_PATH =
  <root>/package.json`; `merge-dev-to-main.sh` does the same; `engine-sync.mjs`
  pins a commit SHA (no version). No shared/release code changed.
- Existing sibling repos are **not** renumbered (verified by reading
  `../tce-*/package.json` — 0.1.17 / 0.1.21 — before and after; no changes).
- Version-neutral re-scaffold of an existing repo is covered by the unit-test
  preserve case (AC2 allows either); a live re-scaffold of a real sibling is
  optional and skipped to avoid churn.
- Gates: `npm test -- --project unit` + `npm run build` pass; full suite
  (`npm test`) run by the test skill before `in_review`.

| AC | Covered by |
|----|-----------|
| 1 no core-version coupling in scaffold (baseline 0.1.0 + preserve) | A, B |
| 2 existing repos not renumbered; re-scaffold version-neutral | D (verify) + unit preserve case (A) |
| 3 scope limited to scaffold seeding; ship path verified only | D |

| 7 full suite passes | D (gates) |

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()`, new
  `GAME_INITIAL_VERSION` + `readExistingPackageVersion()`, `ScaffoldOptions`,
  `ScaffoldResult`, `scaffoldGameRepo()`, CLI output.

- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Build-Time Version Injection.

- Keep the `CoreManifest.version` field typed (subset of package.json) but

- Add an optional explicit `version` override to `ScaffoldOptions` / CLI.

# Manually test the story-line extraction (core + Main Street)

**Goal:** As a developer/QA, manually exercise the extracted generic story-line system and confirm the mechanic behaves exactly as before, that the Gym demo works, and that the documentation matches observable behaviour.

## Context

The branching story-line mechanic was extracted from `tce-main-street` into the generic, game-agnostic `@story-line` module in this repo (see work item `CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B`). Main Street now consumes it through thin adapters. This item is the **manual acceptance pass** that complements the automated parity/full-suite gates.

- Core module: `src/story-line/` (alias `@story-line`).
- Gym demo: `example-games/gym/scenes/GymStorylineScene.ts`.
- Core reference: `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`.
- Consumer: `tce-main-street` at `dev` 87486479 (core submodule `fab1ce28`).

- Core checkout at the current `dev` `fab1ce28`; sibling `tce-main-street` at `dev` 87486479 with its `core` submodule pinned to `fab1ce28` (already the state in this workspace).
- Launch with `GAMES_CONFIG=full npm run dev` so both the Gym and Main Street load in the Game Selector (plain `npm run dev` shows only the Gym). Record the seed when starting a Main Street run so determinism checks (AC 3) can be reproduced.
- Record the exact steps taken, observed results, build/commit tested, and any screenshots or notes in a comment before closing.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Gym demo walkthrough.** Run `npm install && npm run dev`, open the Gym, select **Storyline**, and verify:
  - the Town Meeting card presents **Invest** / **Ignore** with the default UI adapter's choice-clarity labels;
  - choosing **Invest** applies the Town Meeting card's own effect (Lose 50 coins, −50) and deals **Public Investment**, which offers **Celebrate** / **Double down**;
  - choosing **Celebrate** applies Public Investment's +120 coins and deals the terminal **New Beginning** card; **New Beginning** (no options) applies its +60 reputation effect and ends the chain ("Chain complete");
  - a terminal option (**Double down** / **Let it be**) ends the chain immediately with no successor;
  - **Reset** restarts the demo from Town Meeting; the journal/status panel tracks the choices.
- **Main Street shipped storylines.** In `tce-main-street`, play each of the five shipped arcs (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) and verify manually:
  - the dialog title is the storyline name and the subtitle is the incident name;
  - the option labels and choice-clarity labels match the documented semantics (apply vs skip, no escalation card revealed);

- New storyline authoring / conditional options (tracked separately).

# Intake Brief: Visual storyline authoring editor (core)

**Recreated in the core repo.** This epic was moved from `tce-main-street`
(`MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19`, deleted on migration) because the story-line engine now
lives in core (`src/story-line/`, shipped by `CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B`). The
original producer decisions are carried forward unchanged: **Q1 = A (in-repo
local web tool)**, **Q2 = A (epic decomposed into vertical slices)**, **Q3 = A
(curated form/guided editor)**.

## Problem statement

The branching story-line mechanic is now a first-class core module
(`src/story-line/`: types, `compile`, `resolve`, `journal`, `ui-adapter`, plus
the `@story-line` alias and the Gym `GymStorylineScene` demo). What did **not**
move is authoring: the content CSV model, the transactional author API, the
static validator and the manifest/Mermaid graph generator are still
Main-Street-only code (`tce-main-street` `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts`,
`validate-storylines.ts`, `storyline-graph.ts`, `render-storyline-graph.ts`)
wired to Main Street card columns (coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`,
`storylineTitle`).

Consequently a content designer for **any** TCE game that uses story-lines can
still only hand-edit a game-local CSV or drive a game-local CLI, and can only
see the arc as a generated Mermaid/JSON/`SVG` artefact. They cannot *see* the arc
they are editing, cannot discover dangling targets visually, and cannot make a
guided, validated edit in one place.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers (any TCE game)** — see a storyline's shape at
  a glance, inspect a card's links and metadata, and make guided edits (rename,
  retarget a link, regroup a storyline, add a card) without touching CSV
  internals.
- **TCE core engineers** — trust that every edit goes through one validated,
  transactional write path and that committed artefacts stay in sync with the
  game's content CSV.
- **Future tooling authors** — reuse an editor/view-model seam that reads the
  manifest rather than re-parsing the CSV.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to open a local tool, see the storyline graph
  rendered from the manifest, and click a card to inspect its links, so I can
  understand an arc before changing it."
- "As a content designer, I want to edit a card's name, effect and successor
  links in a form and see a preview plus validation errors, so I cannot write a
  dangling chain."
- "As a content designer, I want the committed graph and manifest regenerated
  automatically after an accepted edit, so the docs never drift from content."
- "As a game developer, I want the editor to be a local dev tool driven by my
  game's content adapter, excluded from the game build and reusing the same
  author API, so it adds no runtime dependency and no second CSV write path."

## Scope areas

### 0. Content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (prerequisite)

The editor must not depend on Main-Street-only code, so the authoring seams the
original epic assumed are part of this epic's scope:

1. A generic **content model** over the core story-line types: parse/serialise
   the game content CSV, a **content adapter** seam for game-specific columns
   (Main Street's coins/reputation deltas, `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`,
   `hasChoices`/accept/reject), and a content checksum for change detection.
2. A generic **manifest builder** and Mermaid **graph generator** (deterministic,
   timestamp-free) producing the same node/edge/storyline/cycle shape the
   editor's view model consumes.
3. A generic **static validator** with a formattable report (cycles
   informational, opt-in failure on cycle).
4. A generic **transactional author API**: build the edited CSV in memory,
   validate, then write atomically; `--dry-run` supported; the **only** writer.
5. Thin `tsx` CLIs over each seam (core tooling runs on `tsx`, not `vite-node`).

Parity requirement: extracting these seams must not change Main Street's shipped
storylines or CSV formats; the existing Main-Street storyline suites stay green
while it migrates onto the core seams.

### A. Editor host and read-only graph viewer

6. A local web tool launched with `npm run storylines:editor` from the repo
   root, built on the existing Vite toolchain (no new runtime dependency). It is
   a development tool and must not be included in the game or Electron build.
   The tool takes the game's content CSV / adapter as a launch argument so it is
   game-agnostic.
7. An interactive, manifest-driven graph view: storyline grouping, choice cards
   distinguished from plain incidents, cycle edges marked, pan/zoom and node
   selection. Read-only in the first slice.

### B. Transactional write bridge

8. A Node-side bridge over the core author/validator/graph seams: preview/diff
   before write, validate-before-write, artefact regeneration after an accepted
   edit, and a concurrency guard (content hash).

### C. Curated form/guided editing UX

9. Edit an existing card's fields through the content adapter's generic field
   descriptors (core-editable: name, effect text, choice flag, accept/reject
   successor links, storyline id/title; game columns such as coin/reputation
   deltas come from the adapter).
10. Add a new card and link it into a storyline through a guided form; discard
    pending (unwritten) changes before committing.

### D. Storyline management, docs and tests

11. Storyline-level operations (create/rename a `storylineId`/`storylineTitle`
    group and reassign member cards) driven through the same author API.
12. Documentation covering launch, the viewer, the edit workflow, validation and
    artefact regeneration (core engine reference + developer tooling docs), and
    the note in `tce-main-street` that its authoring tooling now consumes core.
13. Unit tests for the view-model/API bridge and a browser (Playwright) test for
    the viewer and a representative edit round-trip.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Editor launches locally** — `npm run storylines:editor -- --help` exits 0
   from the core repo root on the existing toolchain with no new runtime
   dependency; the command is documented in the core docs. Verified by a test
   that invokes the entry point and asserts it exits 0.
2. **Game-agnostic content source** — the editor loads a game's content CSV and
   field mapping through the content adapter; no Main Street import appears in
   the editor or the core authoring seams. Verified by a unit test over a
   synthetic fixture plus an import-boundary check.
3. **Manifest-driven interactive graph** — the editor renders the generated
   manifest: all nodes and edges appear, choice cards are visually distinct,
   storyline grouping and cycle edges are shown, and selecting a node shows its
   links/metadata. Covered by a browser test.
4. **Read-only fidelity** — the editor's view model (nodes, edges, storyline
   ids/titles, cycle flags) matches the generated manifest exactly; verified by
   a unit test that diffs the view model against the manifest and its JSON
   schema.
5. **Curated editing via the author API only** — the editor can edit the fields
   in Scope C and add a card; every mutation is routed through the core author
   API. A test asserts no editor module writes the content CSV except through
   that module, and a round-trip test proves an edited fixture validates.
6. **Preview and validate-before-write** — every edit shows a preview/diff and
   runs the validator before writing; an invalid edit exits non-zero, writes
   nothing, and surfaces the offending card/link. Covered by unit tests against
   valid and deliberately broken edits.
7. **Artefacts regenerated on accepted edit** — after an accepted edit the tool
   regenerates the committed Mermaid/JSON manifest artefacts (and any generated
   per-game doc artefacts the game opts into), and the `--check` drift guards
   pass. Edits that touch hand-written documented rows surface an explicit
   "manual documentation update required" result naming the failing check.
   Covered by tests.
8. **Concurrency guard** — if the content CSV changed on disk since load, the
   editor refuses to write and instructs the author to reload. Covered by a
   unit test.
9. **Build excluded** — the editor assets/entry are not part of the production
   game bundle or the packaged Electron app; verified by a build/test assertion
   (the editor entry is not referenced from the game `index.html`/`main.ts`
   graph).

    tooling docs, code comments, and the Main Street note that its authoring
    tooling consumes the core seams.

- **Deterministic artefacts** — manifest/Mermaid generators must stay
  timestamp-free so existing drift guards keep passing.
- **Development tool, not shipped** — the editor must not be pulled into the
  production game build or the packaged Electron app.
- **Behaviour preservation** — extraction must not change Main Street's shipped
  storylines (tax, health, economy, labour, restaurant) or CSV formats; RNG seed
  replays stay identical.
- **Preserve designed tension** — the editor is an authoring tool; it must not
  alter player-facing content semantics or reveal escalation content to players.
- **UK English** in all UI copy and documentation.
- **Scope guard** — conditional/cost-gated option semantics

## Goal

Edits from the editor are routed through the core transactional author API,
previewed and validated before writing, with committed artefacts regenerated and
a concurrency guard preventing lost updates.

## User story

"As a content designer, I want an edit to be previewed and validated before it
is written, so I cannot write a dangling chain or clobber someone else's edit."

## Scope

- `src/story-line/editor/api.ts` — thin bridge over the core seams, reusing their
  exported functions:
  - `src/story-line/content/author.ts` — edit application, `applyToFile`,
    storyline assignment via the card's storyline id/title fields (expose it as a
    single `setStoryline` wrapper for F4).
  - `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — validation + text/JSON reports.
  - `src/story-line/content/manifest.ts` — manifest build, serialise, Mermaid.
  - `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — content checksum.
  Expose `previewEdit`, `validateEdit`, `applyEdit`, `regenerateArtefacts`.
- Host API endpoints in `scripts/storyline-editor-server.ts` (same toolchain as
  the CLI) for preview / validate / apply.
- Diff/preview response: before/after CSV rows for the affected card(s) plus the
  validation report.
- Concurrency guard: content checksum captured at load, compared before any
  write; on mismatch refuse and instruct a reload. Reuse the single checksum
  implementation from the content model — do not invent a second hash.
- All writes go through the author API, which writes atomically after in-memory
  validation; the bridge must not write the CSV itself.
- Artefact regeneration after an accepted edit: rewrite the committed Mermaid
  and JSON manifest artefacts and verify with `--check`.
- Hand-written doc sections are **not** machine-generated. When an edit touches a
  documented row, the bridge must return an explicit "manual documentation update
  required" result naming the check that now fails, instead of claiming the drift
  guard passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every edit returns a preview/diff and runs the validator before writing; an
  invalid edit exits non-zero, leaves the content CSV byte-identical, and
  surfaces the offending card/link.
- After an accepted edit the committed Mermaid/JSON manifest artefacts are
  regenerated and the `--check` drift guards report no drift.
- If the content CSV changed on disk since load, the bridge refuses to write and
  returns a reload instruction (unit test).
- No editor module writes a content CSV except through the core author API; the
  T1 write-path guard passes.
- A round-trip test on a fixture proves a valid edited fixture validates and,
  when the edit changes a hand-documented row, the bridge reports the required
  manual doc update naming the failing check.

## Key Files (predicted)

**Key Files:**

# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

**Goal:** Add cost-gating, extra effects, and declarative conditional successors to the generic story-line option model in core, enabling game authors to express options that are only available when the player can afford them, branch differently based on game state, and carry their own consequences.

## Provenance

Refilled from `tce-main-street` epic **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** after the story-line engine was extracted into this repo's core module (`src/story-line/`). The epic, its plan revision, producer decisions (Q1–Q3), assumptions, and risks are preserved verbatim; only the target paths and scope have been adapted to TCE core.

## What landed before this epic

- The generic story-line engine was extracted to `src/story-line/` with the game-agnostic adapter seam (`@story-line` alias, parity tests, Gym demo): **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B**.
- CSV `options` encoding supports arbitrary labels and candidate sets (`parseStorylineOptionsEncoding`).
- `PendingStorylineChoice.options` provides a draw-time frozen snapshot of the compiled option list.

## Existing state (verified against `src/story-line/`)

- `StorylineOption` (`src/story-line/types.ts`) carries `label`, `successorId?`, `successorIds?`, `effectPolicy`, `condition?`, `successorResolver?`.
- `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `compileStorylineFromEvent()` (`src/story-line/compile.ts`) compiles registry > CSV > legacy, with draw-time `condition` filtering.
- `resolveStorylineOption()` (`src/story-line/resolve.ts`) applies `effectPolicy`, resolves successor with documented precedence (callback > random draw > single id), computes deltas via `adapter.getResources(state)` before/after.
- `createPendingStorylineChoice()` / `getPendingStorylineOptions()` (`src/story-line/index.ts`) manage the pending-choice lifecycle with a draw-time snapshot.
- `StorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/story-line/types.ts`) provides `rng()`, `applyEffect()`, `getResources()`, `appendLog()`, etc. — the **only** path from core into game state.
- None of `cost`, `extraEffect`, or `conditionalSuccessors` exists anywhere in `src/story-line/` — these are genuine remaining gaps.

## Desired change

Extend the in-memory model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional declarative affordability `cost`; the draw-time presented list additionally filters out unaffordable options.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered declarative `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time.
3. Selection applies `effectPolicy` (unchanged), deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently, and pushes the resolver-precedence successor.
4. A `validateStorylineOptions()` helper validates cost/extra-effect/condition data; the Gym demo remains a green smoke test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional `cost`, `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors` fields; omitting preserves current behaviour.
2. **Cost gating.** Options whose `cost.coins` exceeds `getResources(state).coins`, or whose `cost.reputation` exceeds `getResources(state).reputation`, are omitted from the presented list; no-cost options always included.
3. **Presented list stability.** `PendingStorylineChoice.options` stores the draw-time snapshot populated at choice draw time; the presented list is computed once at draw and is stable.
4. **Cost deduction.** Selecting an affordable option deducts cost coins and cost reputation from `state` via the engine adapter's resource-mutation seam.
5. **Extra effects.** Any `extraEffect` is applied after cost deduction, independently of `effectPolicy`; both can coexist.
6. **Loss checks and logging.** Cost deduction and extra effects are reported in `coinChange`/`repChange` deltas; `appendLog()` captures the operations. Consumer-side loss checks fire when resources drop to zero (unchanged).
7. **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` evaluated sequentially; first rule matching `getResources(state)` determines pushed card ID; `successorId` fallback.
8. **Boundary coverage.** All boundary cases tested: above/below threshold, equality boundary, no-match fallback; matched successor via `pushChainCard`.
9. **Precedence.** `successorResolver` callback wins when present; otherwise conditional rules run before `successorIds` random draw and legacy `successorId`; a matching rule consumes no RNG draw.
10. **Cost-aware consumer scoring.** The `getPendingStorylineOptions` snapshot gives consumers (e.g. Main Street AI) the cost-filtered list to score — no core AI in scope.
11. **Determinism.** All new semantics are pure/declarative; no new RNG. Gym demo runs to completion without stalls.
12. **Static validation.** `validateStorylineOptions()` rejects negative/zero costs; unknown field or op; non-numeric value; negative extraEffect; dangling conditional successors.
13. **Shipped content.** Existing CSV-encoded cards, Gym fixtures, and parity tests validate cleanly; the doc-drift / docs-consistency test passes.
14. **Documentation.** `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` documents the extended `StorylineOption` fields, cost filtering, extra effects, conditional successors, and resolution lifecycle with examples.
15. **Seam and authoring docs.** `src/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` confirm new semantics are programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`, not CSV-authored.
16. **Parity regression.** All existing unit/smoke/parity tests remain green with zero behavioural deltas.

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the in-memory model, engine resolution, and validator. The CSV `options` column does not gain cost/extra-effect/conditional authoring — those stay programmatic via `registerStorylineOptions`.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics live behind `StorylineEngineAdapter` and keep the module determinism intact.
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** All specified costs must be affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are removed from the presented list.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted in addition to the option's effectPolicy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- **Full suite gate.** Every child's DoD includes a green full project test suite (`npx vitest run --project unit`); the epic is not complete until all parity/regression tests pass with zero behavioural deltas.

## Core adaptation notes

These differences from the original Main Street epic must be resolved during implementation:

- **Resource mutation seam.** `StorylineEngineAdapter` has `getResources(state)` but no `applyResourceDelta(state, { coins, reputation })` method. Cost deduction and extra effects require extending the adapter. **Design option:** add an optional `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter interface (with a default no-op for existing implementors) so core remains compatible. The child items document this as an open design note.
- **Resources at compile time.** `compileStorylineFromEvent(event, registry, state)` currently receives only `state` for condition callbacks; cost filtering needs `getResources(state)`. The `createPendingStorylineChoice()` wrapper (which has the full `StorylineSystem` instance) can supply an optional `getResources` function or extend the signature.
- **No AI in core.** `decideEventChoice` (Main Street AI scoring) is a consumer concern. The core module provides the cost-filtered snapshot via `getPendingStorylineOptions`; Main Street updates its AI to read it. Tracked separately as **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9-C7**.
- **No CSV pipeline/validator in core.** `validateStorylineOptions()` validates registered/compiled options programmatically. JSON schema and `storyline-graph.ts` are Main Street concerns.
- **Docs location.** Canonical docs at `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (not `docs/game/`).

## Risks

- **Adapter API change.** Extending `StorylineEngineAdapter` with `applyResourceDelta` is a breaking change for existing adapter implementors (Main Street, Gym). *Mitigation:* optional method with sensible default, migration note, and parity gate.
- **Cost filtering changes the index space.** The draw-time snapshot (`PendingStorylineChoice.options`) already freezes the presented list, so cost filtering inherits that stability — but consumers must read the snapshot. *Mitigation:* `getPendingStorylineOptions` returns the cost-filtered snapshot; parity/regression tests cover this.
- **Precedence ambiguity.** Two successor mechanisms now coexist (callback resolver, declarative rules) plus random candidate sets. *Mitigation:* precedence documented in code and tests (callback > declarative rules > random candidates > single successor).
- **Scope creep.** Callback conditions/resolvers already ship; CSV label authoring already shipped. This work adds only cost/extraEffect/conditionalSuccessors.

---

## Producer decisions (preserved from original)

- **Q1=A** — Programmatic only; no CSV column authoring.
- **Q2.1** — Gates: coins and/or reputation.
- **Q2.2** — Omitted, not disabled.
- **Q2.3** — Real payment (deducted in addition to effectPolicy).
- **Q3=A** — Declarative, serialisable data.

## Plan summary

| # | Child | Title | Dependency |
|---|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | C1 | Extend StorylineOption model with cost, extraEffect, conditionalSuccessors | (none) |
| 2 | C2 | Add cost-based affordability filtering at draw time | C1 |
| 3 | C3 | Deduct cost and apply extra effects at resolution | C1, C2 |
| 4 | C4 | Resolve declarative conditional successors | C1, C2, C3 |
| 5 | C5 | Validate declarative option metadata (new helper + tests) | C1, C4 |
| 6 | C6 | Update documentation for extended option model | C3, C4, C5 |

## Related work

- **CG-0MVH2H67H002M27B** — Generic story-line system in core (completed; parent context for this extension).
- **MS-0MUNB58TK0025CB9** — Original epic in Main Street (being deleted after refile).

## Problem statement

`scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` decides whether a non-zero Vitest run is recoverable (retry) or acceptable (green) purely from the run's **output text**: a transient contention signature (`[vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"`, `[vitest] Browser connection was closed while running tests`) plus an all-passed summary (`Test Files N passed (N)`) is treated as `accepted-transient` (exit 0). The runner has no notion of *which files the run intended to execute*, so a run that silently dropped part of the suite can be accepted as green.

Discovered during MS-0MVK37SK5009M0NG (tce-main-street): the serialized `unit-cli` project was silently skipped. Root cause there: Vitest 3.2.7's `executeTests` group loop aborts when an earlier `sequence.groupOrder` group's pool run rejects, dropping every later group while still summarising the executed files as green. That repo fixed the cause (serialized group now runs first) and added a spec-driven zero-coverage reporter guard.

Residual gap (engine-side): when a transient occurs on **both** attempts *and* files were dropped, the summary still reads `Test Files N passed (N)`, so `shouldRetryOnce` returns true and the second attempt is `accepted-transient`. A consumer-repo reporter cannot defeat this: it can only set `process.exitCode` / print an error, both of which the acceptance path ignores.

## Users and user stories

**Primary user — agent/CI gate operator (and the audits that read the gate's cache).**

- As an agent running the full suite before a push, I want a run that silently executed only part of the suite to fail loudly with the names of the files that never ran, so a false green can never reach `dev`.
- As an audit consumer of the full-suite cache, I want the gate's acceptance decision to be auditable (expected vs executed counts in the summary line), so I can tell a genuine full-suite green from a recovered transient.
- As an engine maintainer, I want the expectation to be self-deriving from the Vitest project configuration, so adding or renaming a test file never requires editing the runner or ~20 call sites.

**Secondary user — consumer repos (e.g. `tce-main-street`)** composing the core runner: they keep today's behaviour unless they explicitly opt in, and they can pin an explicit file list via the low-level seam when their layout is non-standard.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The runner accepts an **opt-in** expectation of the test-file set through two surfaces:
   - repeatable `--expected-file <path>` (low-level, deterministic seam, primarily for tests and non-standard layouts), and
   - `--expect-project-coverage` (derives the expected set from a pre-flight collection-only `vitest list --filesOnly --json` over the forwarded project/args).
2. When an expectation is supplied, a run whose executed file set **differs** from the expected set (missing **or** extra files) is a genuine failure: non-zero exit, never `accepted-transient`, never converted to green by the retry — regardless of the run's own exit code (a dropped group can exit 0 with an all-passed summary).
3. The coverage diagnostic (written to stderr, alongside a non-zero exit) names every missing file and every extra file, and states `expected=N ran=M`.
4. When no expectation is supplied (`--expected-file` absent and `--expect-project-coverage` absent), every acceptance decision and exit code is **identical to today**, pinned by regression tests over the existing recorded fixtures.
5. A regression test pins the incident shape: transient signature + `Test Files N passed (N)` + one expected file missing ⇒ non-zero exit, the missing file named in the output, and no `accepted-transient` outcome on either attempt.
6. `runSummary()` records the expectation state (`expected=N ran=M`, or `expected=unset` when no expectation was supplied) so the acceptance decision is auditable.
7. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` passes `--expect-project-coverage` on the **unit** and **browser** stages only; `run-smoke-tests.sh`, `run-dev-tests.sh` and every `/skill:test --type` command remain unchanged (switch off).
8. Hang semantics unchanged: an attempt that exceeds the wall-clock bound still exits 124, is never retried, and is reported as a hang before any coverage check.
9. A pre-flight failure (the `vitest list` collection itself fails, times out, or returns an empty set) **fails closed** with a clear diagnostic — the runner must never silently downgrade to "no expectation" and continue.
10. Documentation is updated to reflect the change (`AGENTS.md` test-execution/quality-gate notes and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` runner/test-profile sections, including the new flags and the `expected=N ran=M` summary field).
11. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Opt-in only.** Default behaviour (no expectation) must be byte-for-byte identical in decisions; the change must not make existing runs stricter for consumer repos that supply nothing.
- **Keep the pure-seam design.** The runner's existing injectable `VitestRunner` seam stays; expectation derivation and file-set comparison must be injectable/pure so unit tests need no real Vitest process, browser, or multi-minute run.
- **No browser launch in pre-flight.** The expected-set collection must use collection-only/static parsing (`--filesOnly --json --staticParse`) so the browser stage does not pay a second Chromium start. If a consumer's Vitest version rejects `--staticParse`, retry once without it before failing closed (the runner is synced into game repos, some of which pin Vitest 3.x).
- **Non-goals (out of scope):** enabling coverage on smoke/dev/skill-typed commands; retrofitting a spec-driven coverage guard into consumer repos; changing `scripts/vitest-tap-reporter.ts`.
- **Version-agnostic guard.** The fix must be set-based, not tied to Vitest internal group ordering (`sequence.groupOrder`, `executeTests`): the engine is on Vitest 4.1.11 while the incident evidence came from 3.2.7. No new Vitest-major-specific API may be load-bearing without the degradation path above.
- **Narrow wiring.** Only `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` (unit + browser) opts in, per the operator decision; no change to smoke/dev/skill-typed command strings in this item.
- UK English, `dev`-only pushes, build → test → commit order.

## Existing state

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (458 lines): `hasTransientSignature()`, `errorBlocks()`, `failuresAreTransientOnly()`, `shouldRetryOnce()`, `runWithRetry()`, `runSummary()`, `runVitestAsync()`, `parseTimeoutArgs()`, `main()`. Acceptance today: `Test Files N passed (N)` in the output ⇒ retry allowed; both attempts transient-only ⇒ exit 0 `accepted-transient`.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`: fixtures for the clean, failed-file, browser-drop, all-failed, missing-summary and hang shapes; asserts retry/acceptance decisions and `runSummary()` formatting. This is where the new regression test belongs.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` line ~65 (`--project unit --timeout-ms 300000`) and ~69 (`--project browser --timeout-ms 1200000`) are the two in-scope call sites.
- `scripts/vitest-tap-reporter.ts` emits flat TAP for triage only; it is not an authoritative source of the executed-file set.
- Verified during intake: `npx vitest list --project unit --filesOnly --json --staticParse` (Vitest 4.1.11) prints `[{ "file": "<abs path>", "projectName": "unit" }, …]` — a usable expectation source.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` lists `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` among synced files — check whether the change affects consumer-repo syncing.

## Desired change

1. **Argument parsing** — extend the runner's own flag parsing (`--timeout-ms` style) with `--expected-file <path>` (repeatable, also `--expected-file=<path>`) and `--expect-project-coverage`; both consumed by the runner and removed from the forwarded Vitest args.
2. **Expected-set derivation** — collection-only `vitest list --filesOnly --json [<forwarded filters>]`, normalised to repo-relative POSIX paths; injected command runner for unit tests. Fail closed on error, timeout or empty set (`expected=0` is only acceptable when the run also executed zero files *and* the project genuinely has none — otherwise a diagnostic failure).
3. **Executed-set capture** — capture the set of files the attempt actually executed (preferred: the runner injects its own `--reporter=json` + `--outputFile.json=<tempfile>` so the set is exact and independent of the caller's reporters; the temp file is removed after the attempt). Fall back to parsing default-reporter per-file lines only if the artefact is missing, and treat "expectation supplied but executed set indeterminable" as a genuine failure rather than green.
4. **Coverage gate in `runWithRetry`** — new expectation parameter; the coverage comparison runs on the first attempt *before* the retry decision and again on the second attempt before any acceptance, so a coverage violation can never be masked by `accepted-transient` or by a clean retry.
5. **Auditable summary** — `runSummary()` gains `expected=N ran=M` (or `expected=unset`), plus distinct outcomes (`coverage-failed`, `retry-clean-covered`, …) as appropriate; existing outcome strings for expectation-free runs stay unchanged so downstream parsers keep working.
6. **Tests** — extend `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts`: expectation-free parity (AC 4), missing-file ⇒ fail + named file + no acceptance (AC 5), extra-file ⇒ fail (AC 2/3), flag parsing, fail-closed pre-flight, hang precedence (AC 8), `runSummary()` expectation fields (AC 6).
7. **Wiring + docs** — add `--expect-project-coverage` to the two `run-ci-tests.sh` invocations; update `AGENTS.md` (test-execution policy / quality gates) and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (retry runner + profile tables).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — flag parsing for the expectation, collection-only derivation, executed-set capture, coverage gate in `runWithRetry`, `runSummary()` field, coverage diagnostic message.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — new regression suite (parity, missing/extra file, fail-closed pre-flight, hang precedence, summary format).
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — pass `--expect-project-coverage` to the unit and browser stages; header comment update.
- `AGENTS.md` — test-execution policy + quality-gate wording (runner derives and enforces project coverage on the CI stages).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — retry-runner and test-profile sections: new flags, fail-closed behaviour, `expected=N ran=M` summary field.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — verify whether the runner's consumer-sync entry needs any change (probably none; the runner is synced into game repos, so the opt-in default matters).
- `scripts/check-browser-test-env.ts` — read-only reference for the "pre-flight pre-check" idiom and its unit-test style; expected to need no change.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (verified):** `vitest list --filesOnly --json --staticParse` is available and returns absolute `file` paths on Vitest 4.1.11.
- **Assumption:** injecting a JSON reporter with `--outputFile.json` composes with the default reporter and does not disturb the `Test Files N passed (N)` detection. If it does, the fallback is default-reporter line parsing (weaker but sufficient for the CI stages, which use the default reporter).
- **Risk — stale expectation:** derived at the same commit, so a mismatch is a real defect; but a *dynamic* test file (e.g. a generated project) could legitimately differ. Mitigation: fail closed with a clear diagnostic rather than silently tolerating.
- **Risk — pre-flight cost:** a static-parse list adds a few seconds per stage; bounded with its own timeout so it can never hang the gate.
- **Risk — `--project` wildcards/filters:** derivation must forward the caller's filters so project subsets resolve identically; a mismatch here would produce spurious coverage failures. Mitigation: unit tests with injected list output.
- **Risk — shared runner across repos:** `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` syncs `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` into game repos, some on Vitest 3.x. The switch being off by default keeps them unchanged; the documented `--staticParse` degradation (and its own unit test) keeps opt-in usable there. Any residual version gap is recorded as a follow-up work item, not widened here.
- **Risk — scope creep:** enabling coverage on smoke/dev/skill-typed commands, or retrofitting a spec-driven coverage guard into consumer repos, is out of scope — record as follow-up work items if opportunities arise.
- **Risk — masking by design:** if the executed-set capture silently returns "unknown" and the code treats that as "no expectation", the whole fix evaporates. Mitigation: explicit "expectation supplied but unverifiable ⇒ fail" rule + regression test (AC 9).

## Related work

- MS-0MVK37SK5009M0NG (tce-main-street) — root-cause analysis, evidence, and the consumer-side fix (serialized group first) + spec-driven zero-coverage reporter guard. This item closes the residual engine-side gap that a consumer reporter cannot reach.
- CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F — attribution-aware masking guard (`failuresAreTransientOnly`) that the acceptance path currently relies on.
- CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU — the "both attempts transient ⇒ accept green" rule that this item narrows when coverage data exists.
- CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N — wall-clock hang timeout whose semantics (exit 124, never retried) must be preserved.
- CG-0MUECQ22U002Z0A1 / CG-0MUDYCJUC009URD6 — `scripts/vitest-tap-reporter.ts` and its parent (triage TAP bridge); clarifies why the tap reporter is not a coverage oracle.
- CG-0MT022826006EM0D — PR CI gated on build only; raises the stakes on the local full-suite gate this runner protects.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md#testing` (runner/retry + test-profile tables) and `AGENTS.md` **Test execution policy** / **Quality Gates** — the documentation surfaces this change must keep accurate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- Q1: "How should the runner learn the expected file set — (a) repeatable `--expected-file` flags from each caller, (b) self-derive via a cheap pre-flight `vitest list --json` behind one opt-in switch, or (c) a committed per-project expectation spec file?" — Answer (Map/producer): **(b)**. Rationale recorded: self-maintaining, no per-caller enumeration; the low-level `--expected-file` seam is retained for tests and non-standard layouts. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Which callers should switch it on in this item — (a) none, (b) `run-ci-tests.sh` unit + browser only, (c) also smoke/dev and the `/skill:test --type` commands?" — Answer (Map/producer): **(b)**. Rationale: fixes the gate that was actually fooled, keeps blast radius small; broadening is a follow-up if stable. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Mismatch semantics when expectation data is supplied — (a) fail only when fewer files ran, (b) fail on any set difference (name missing files, also name extras)?" — Answer (Map/producer): **(b)**. Rationale: a stale or mis-scoped expectation is itself a defect; at a fixed commit a set difference is unambiguous. Source: interactive reply.

Curated after review — the keyword sweep matched three unrelated completed `MainStreetLifecycleManager.ts` parse-error items (CG-0MSXL3SUX009TFVZ, CG-0MSXL3TP0003RVAC, CG-0MSXL3U43006N8Y6); they share no acceptance criteria with this item and are excluded per the conservative-reporting policy. ## Problem statement

Under CPU contention the Vitest **browser** stage can fail with

    Error: Failed to import test file <path>
    Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:<port>/<path>

while every other file passes and the same files pass on a quiet machine. That is
the Vite dev server failing to serve a module under load — the same class of
transient contention failure as the worker-RPC timeout and the browser WebSocket
drop that `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` already retries — but it is not in the
runner's recognised signature set, so the run is never retried and the gate fails
spuriously.

## Users

- **Producer / release engineer** running `/skill:test` or `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  on a loaded workstation: "When the only thing that broke is the vite dev server
  dropping a module fetch under load, I want one automatic retry instead of
  re-running a 20-minute suite by hand."
- **Agent implementing a work item**: "I need the push gate to be a verdict about
  my code, not about ambient CPU contention."
- **Maintainer of the retry runner**: "I need the new signature to stay inside the
  existing attribution discipline, so a real broken import is never excused."

## Acceptance Criteria

- A browser run whose only errors are the module-fetch signature
  (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`) is retried **exactly once**, and
  accepted as green only when the retry is clean (exit 0 / all files passed).
- Acceptance of this signature requires the retry to be green: a run where **both**
  attempts show the module-fetch signature is reported as a failure and never
  `accepted-transient`. A genuine module-resolution regression (mistyped import
  path, deleted file, 404 on an asset module) is deterministic and must surface.
  The existing all-passed-signature acceptance path (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU) is
  unchanged for the two original signatures.
- A run containing any error that is not attributable to a transient signature
  (e.g. an `AssertionError`, or a `Failed to import test file` block without the
  module-fetch cause) is never retried and never accepted as green.
- The signature is a named exported constant
  (`MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`) and is documented in the runner header comment as a
  fourth contention signature alongside the existing three (worker RPC timeout,
  browser WebSocket drop, true hang), with the same "every error block must
  contain it" attribution rule (`failuresAreTransientOnly`).
- Project-coverage semantics are unchanged: acceptance still requires the executed
  file set to match the expectation, and it is verified (unit test or documented
  reasoning) that a failed-to-import file still appears in the captured executed
  set so the coverage gate does not turn the retried-green run into a
  `[coverage-failed]` exit.
- Unit tests in `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` cover: positive
  (module-fetch-only failing run retried, clean retry returns the retry's status),
  both-attempts (not accepted, `outcome=retry-failed`/`failed`), and negative
  (module-fetch signature alongside a genuine assertion failure → no retry).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code
  comments, the runner header, `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`'s header comment,
  `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (both enumerate the transient signatures).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` is the runner's own regression
  suite; the new fixtures must be additive and must not weaken the existing
  masking-guard pins (including the verbatim CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F incident
  fixture).
- The runner must stay byte-for-byte identical in behaviour when no expectation
  is supplied and no transient signature is present (no change to exit codes for
  genuine failures).
- No product/runtime code changes — this is test-tooling robustness only.
- Fix must not require Vitest/Vite configuration changes (the failure is a
  loaded-machine artefact, not a misconfiguration).
- Matching is Chrome/Chromium-specific text (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported
  module:`); Firefox emits a different message. Scope the constant to the Chromium
  text that the browser project actually uses, and note the limitation in a
  comment rather than inventing an untested pattern.

## Existing state

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` recognises exactly two transient signatures
  (`WORKER_TIMEOUT_SIGNATURE`, `BROWSER_DROP_SIGNATURE`) via
  `hasTransientSignature` / `failuresAreTransientOnly`, plus the third
  (non-retryable) hang signature detected by the wall-clock bound.
- `shouldRetryOnce` retries when the summary is all-passed plus a transient
  signature, or when failures exist but every error block is attributable to a
  transient signature; if the retry is also purely transient the run is accepted
  (CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU).
- The opt-in project-coverage gate (`--expect-project-coverage`, on for the unit
  and browser stages) makes a file-set mismatch a genuine failure.
- Incident evidence (CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD, commit `f9762665`, load avg ~8):
  `tests/core-engine/tf-runtime-integration.browser.test.ts` failed to import and
  `tests/handView/gym-handpile-outlines.browser.test.ts` had 4 tests fail to fetch
  `example-games/gym/createGymHandPileGame.ts`; `attempts=1 outcome=failed`; the
  same commit's browser stage passed 37/37 files on a quiet machine.

## Desired change

1. Add `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE` (`Failed to fetch dynamically imported module`) as
   an exported constant beside the two existing signatures, with the incident
   shape documented in the header comment as signature 4.
2. Extend the attribution predicates so this signature makes a run retryable under
   the same every-error-block rule.
3. Keep acceptance of a both-attempts-poisoned run limited to the pre-existing
   signatures: the new signature is **retry-only** recovery, so the retry's own
   exit status stands.
4. Add positive / both-attempts / negative fixtures and tests to the runner suite.
5. Update the signature enumerations in the runner header,
   `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `AGENTS.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` — add `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`, extend
  `hasTransientSignature` / `failuresAreTransientOnly`, restrict the
  both-attempts acceptance path, update the header comment.
- `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` — new fixtures
  (module-fetch-only failing run, both-attempts variant, genuine-assertion
  counter-case) and the corresponding `shouldRetryOnce` / `runWithRetry` tests.
- `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` — header comment enumerating the transient signatures.
- `AGENTS.md` — testing section ("retries once on Vitest's transient
  contention-induced failures …") must list the new signature.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — `#### CPU-contention mitigation (unit and browser tests)`
  section (signature list, `shouldRetryOnce` shape list, acceptance rule).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Masking risk (primary).** A genuine broken import emits the identical text.
  Mitigation: retry-only recovery plus the every-error-block attribution rule; the
  both-attempts acceptance path is deliberately *not* extended.
- **Coverage-gate interaction.** If a failed-to-import file were absent from the
  JSON reporter's executed set, the coverage gate would reject the run regardless
  of the new signature; the incident summary (`Test Files 1 failed`) suggests it is
  counted, but implementation must confirm the executed-set capture still matches.
- **Pattern brittleness.** Chromium's message may change or Firefox may be used;
  pin the exact Chromium substring and keep the unit fixtures as the contract.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Broader HTTP-level retries (dev-server 5xx, asset 404s),
  `webServer` timeout tuning, and generic "any import failure is transient" logic
  are out of scope; file them as separate work items if they prove needed.
- **Assumption:** the incident is contention-triggered, not a code defect — the
  same commit's browser stage passed 37/37 files on a quiet machine.

## Related work

Manual context (the automated find-related report is appended below):

- CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD — the run that surfaced the gap (story-line management UI).
- CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F — attributable failed-file transient (retry discipline).
- CG-0MUF0LU4X006IXXU — accept when both attempts are pure transient.
- CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N — wall-clock hang bound (never retried).
- CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H — project-coverage gate.
- CG-0MS9M5UJP005PWD3, CG-0MSCI73RH004VPCE — the original two signatures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview round was required.** The item's goal, incident evidence and
  acceptance criteria already resolved the two decisions that would otherwise
  have been asked:
  1. *Does the new signature get the both-attempts acceptance path?* — Answered by
     AC "accepted when the retry is green" plus Scope's "a genuine
     module-resolution regression is never masked": **no**, retry-only recovery.
     Recorded as an explicit AC bullet so the decision is auditable.
  2. *Chromium-only, or a cross-browser pattern?* — Answered by repo search: the
     browser project runs headless Chromium only
     (`scripts/check-browser-test-env.ts`), so the Chromium text is the contract.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping item found (`wl search` on
  "dynamic import transient retry" and "Failed to fetch dynamically imported
  module"; only this item and unrelated completed work matched).
## Implementation notes (plan review)

Planning is auto-completed for this item: the description already carries
measurable acceptance criteria, a five-step desired-change sketch and a
validated `**Key Files**` list (all five paths exist), so no child
decomposition is needed — the change is one coherent edit across the runner,
its regression suite and three documentation surfaces (effort Small, risk
Medium). Details below are intent-preserving notes for the implementer; none
of them changes an acceptance criterion.

1. **Acceptance predicate split.** `runWithRetry` currently reuses
   `shouldRetryOnce(second.result.output)` for the both-attempts
   `accepted-transient` path. Retry-only recovery therefore needs a *separate*
   acceptance predicate (restricted to `WORKER_TIMEOUT_SIGNATURE` and
   `BROWSER_DROP_SIGNATURE`), while `hasTransientSignature` /
   `failuresAreTransientOnly` gain `MODULE_FETCH_SIGNATURE`. A module-fetch
   failure on both attempts must then fall through to `outcome=retry-failed`
   carrying the retry's exit status.
2. **Retry-banner wording.** The `[retry]` message hard-codes
   "(worker RPC timeout or browser connection drop)"; extend it (and the
   `[transient-accepted]` / header text as applicable) so the diagnostic does
   not contradict the recognised signature set.
3. **Verify the real error-block shape.** `errorBlocks()` starts a block at
   each `…Error:` line and `failuresAreTransientOnly()` requires *every* block
   to contain a signature. The incident shape is
   `Error: Failed to import test file <path>` followed by
   `Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: …`. If
   Vitest prints the cause on its own line starting with `TypeError:`, the
   header block would carry no signature and the run would never be retried.
   Pin the verbatim shape in the fixture and, if the cause is a separate block,
   document the attribution treatment chosen in the runner header and cover it
   with a test.
4. **Coverage-gate evidence.** The acceptance criterion requires showing that a
   failed-to-import file still appears in the captured executed set; record that
   evidence (test or documented reasoning) alongside the runner's coverage-gate
   comment.

## OPEN QUESTION: exact Vitest error-block shape for the module-fetch incident

Directed to: whoever holds the CI log for CG-0MVHZ2RBJ004O0VD (commit
`f9762665`). Why it matters: attribution only retries when *every* error block
contains the signature, so if `Caused by: TypeError: …` is emitted as a block
of its own the header block is unattributable and the new signature would never
trigger a retry. Resolution is evidence-gathering only (capture the verbatim
output as a fixture); the acceptance criteria are unchanged.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MT00JNOP003KVH8** – Split non-tutorial browser test suite into per-instance chunks to fix CI context-exhaustion regression (completed)
- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** – Browser test stage hangs on gym overlay tests during full-suite npm test under CPU contention (completed)
- **CG-0MUIMM28K001W88F** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0ms9m5ujp005pwd3, 0msci73rh004vpce, 0mt08r2qr0070f3n, 0muf0lu4x006ixxu, 0muimm28k001w88f (+320 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: 0mt08r2qr0070f3n, 0muf0lu4x006ixxu, 0muimm28k001w88f, 0mvl21cvm003vk5h, absent (+266 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0ms9m5ujp005pwd3, 0msci73rh004vpce, accept, actually, add (+190 more)

discovered-from (cross-repo): MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX in tce-main-street — the engine pin lags the core dev tip, so engine:verify throws PIN MISMATCH on a clean dev checkout (indistinguishable from real drift).

## Chosen policy (producer decision, tce-main-street MS-0MVN1OAG1005JWFX)

The pin **tracks the core dev tip**: a pin that lags the tip is a genuine failure that must be re-pinned, not tolerated. Today nothing writes the pin except a manual release-time edit, so it lags whenever engine dev advances (observed: pin 9ee194e0 vs tip 1c9900a1) and every release needs a hand re-pin (tce-main-street commit 13e7283b). That manual step has already produced a pin/gitlink mismatch bug (MS-0MVMOH2N3000T63F) and a false-drift misdiagnosis.

## Desired change

1. `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` `syncEngine`: when it actually advances `./core`, also write `configs/engine-pin.json` to the new SHA and stage `core` + the pin together, so the two can never diverge in a commit. Offline fallback (remote unreachable, checkout kept) must leave the pin untouched. No-pin-config game repos (no `configs/` dir) must not gain a spurious file — decide behaviour explicitly and document it.
2. `verifyEngine` diagnostics: distinguish **lag** (pin resolves on the tracked branch and is an ancestor of the tip → message says the pin lags by N commits and must be re-pinned; pin + gitlink travel together) from **bad/foreign pin** (pin does not resolve on the tracked branch at all). Keep the hard failure for both; only the diagnosis and next-step text differ.
3. Update `scripts/engine-sync.d.mts` types + `docs/DEVELOPER.md` §"Engine sync/verify scripts in generated game repos" to state the pin-tracks-the-tip policy.
4. Tests in `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` (local `file://` submodule fixtures, no network): sync advances → pin written and equal to the new gitlink; sync no-op → pin untouched; offline fallback → pin untouched; verify with a lagging pin → lag diagnosis; verify with an off-branch pin → bad-pin diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a clean submodule, `sync` that advances the checkout writes `configs/engine-pin.json` to exactly the new HEAD and stages it alongside the `core` gitlink; a second no-op sync leaves the pin byte-identical.
- Offline-fallback sync does not modify the pin (asserted by test).
- `verify` fails with a lag-specific message when the pin is an ancestor of the tracked branch tip, and with a bad-pin message when the pin is not on the branch; both still exit non-zero (asserted by tests).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` states the pin-tracks-the-tip policy and the re-pin behaviour.
- Engine-side `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` covers the new behaviour offline.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
